facts.fact: Peter Jacobsen and Jim Hardy with Ken Kavanaugh, 1992, on the slopes of Pete's Mountain above the Willamette.
Oregon grape was named the state flower in 1899; it grows as an understory shrub in conifer forests.

current.subject: A great blue heron in tall golden grass.
current.weaknesses: The grass hides half the bird; neck and bill are lost at 1x.

concepts.name: The Heron
concepts.rationale: The heron alone, standing in still water: blue-grey body, white face, black crown stripe, dagger bill.
concepts.tradeoffs: Herons are common in golf and lake-club logos.

concepts.name: Oregon Grape
concepts.rationale: A club named for the state carries the state flower: a bunch of dusty blue berries under a spiny leaf.
concepts.strengths: Ownable and on-name; strong colour on green cards.
concepts.tradeoffs: Reads as 'grapes' first; few know the plant.

recommendation: Concept 1. The cleaned-up heron keeps the developer's subject and is the better silhouette; Oregon grape is a clever second.
